title: Task Manager Not Opening
problem: Clicking Task Manager shows nothing or crashes.

fixes.title: Method 1: Keyboard Shortcut
steps: Press and hold the <kbd>Ctrl</kbd> + <kbd>Shift</kbd> + <kbd>Esc</kbd> keys simultaneously.
This key combination bypasses the Start Menu and should force Task Manager to open directly, even if it's not working normally.

fixes.title: Method 2: System File Checker (SFC)
steps: Open Command Prompt as an administrator by searching for 'CMD', right-clicking, and selecting 'Run as administrator'.
Type sfc /scannow and press Enter.
This command will scan all protected system files and replace corrupted files with a cached copy. It can often fix issues with built-in Windows applications like Task Manager.

title: WiFi Connected but No Internet
problem: WiFi shows connected but websites don't load.

fixes.title: Method 1: Reset Winsock Catalog
steps: Open Command Prompt as an administrator.
Type netsh winsock reset and press Enter.
Restart your computer. This command resets the Windows network stack and can fix many connectivity problems.

fixes.title: Method 2: Change DNS Server
steps: Open Network and Sharing Center and navigate to your adapter settings.
Right-click your WiFi adapter, go to 'Properties', then 'Internet Protocol Version 4 (TCP/IPv4)'.
Select 'Use the following DNS server addresses' and enter Google's public DNS: 8.8.8.8 and 8.8.4.4. Click OK.

title: Permission Denied Error
problem: Cannot write or execute files even as root.

fixes.title: Method 1: Check File Ownership
steps: Use the command ls -l filename to view the file's owner and group.
If the owner or group is not correct, use sudo chown newuser:newgroup filename to change them.

fixes.title: Method 2: Grant Execute Permissions
steps: If you need to execute the file, use the command sudo chmod +x filename.
To set specific permissions (read, write, execute), use a numerical code (e.g., chmod 755 filename for read/write/execute for owner, read/execute for group/others).

title: CORS Policy Blocked
problem: API calls fail with 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin' error.

fixes.title: Method 1: Configure Backend Server
steps: On your backend server (e.g., Node.js, Python Flask), you need to set the appropriate CORS headers in the response.
For a development environment, you can set the header to allow all origins: 'Access-Control-Allow-Origin': '*'.
For a production environment, specify the exact domain(s) that should be allowed.

fixes.title: Method 2: Use a Browser Extension (Development Only)
steps: Install a CORS browser extension (e.g., 'CORS Everywhere' for Firefox or 'Moesif CORS' for Chrome).
Enable the extension to bypass CORS policies locally during development and testing.
Remember to disable it for normal Browse and never rely on this for a production application.

title: Slow Startup Time
problem: Computer takes too long to boot up.

fixes.title: Method 1: Disable Startup Programs
steps: Open Task Manager (Ctrl+Shift+Esc) and go to the 'Startup' tab.
Sort by 'Startup impact' and disable any non-essential programs that are high impact. Right-click and select 'Disable'.

fixes.title: Method 2: Perform Disk Cleanup
steps: Open the 'Disk Cleanup' tool by searching for it in the Start Menu.
Select the drive you want to clean (usually C:), then click 'Clean up system files'.
This will remove temporary files, old updates, and other clutter that can slow down your system.

title: Blue Screen of Death (BSOD)
problem: System crashes unexpectedly with a blue screen.

fixes.title: Method 1: Check for Recent Changes
steps: Think about any hardware you've recently installed or any software/driver updates.
If possible, revert the recent changes. For example, uninstall a recently installed driver or remove a new piece of hardware.

fixes.title: Method 2: Run Windows Memory Diagnostic
steps: Search for 'Windows Memory Diagnostic' in the Start Menu and run the application.
Choose to restart your computer and let the tool run a scan for issues with your RAM (Random Access Memory).
Faulty RAM is a common cause of unexpected BSOD errors.

title: Apt-Get Not Working
problem: Cannot install or update packages using apt-get.

fixes.title: Method 1: Check Network Connectivity
steps: Ensure your computer is connected to the internet. You can use ping 8.8.8.8 to test for connectivity.
If there is no connection, check your network configuration or router.

fixes.title: Method 2: Update Package List
steps: The list of available packages might be out of date. Run the command sudo apt-get update to refresh it.
This command fetches the latest information about packages from your configured repositories.

title: Layout Breaks in Mobile
problem: Website looks fine on desktop but is broken on mobile.

fixes.title: Method 1: Check Media Queries
steps: Ensure you have a viewport meta tag in your HTML: <meta name='viewport' content='width=device-width, initial-scale=1.0'>.
In your CSS, check for proper media query breakpoints, such as @media (max-width: 768px), to apply mobile-specific styles.

fixes.title: Method 2: Use Modern Layouts
steps: Prefer using CSS Flexbox or CSS Grid for layout, as they are designed for responsive and flexible design.
Avoid using older techniques like floats and fixed widths, which are not mobile-friendly.

title: Keyboard Shortcuts Not Working
problem: Common keyboard shortcuts like Ctrl+C fail.

fixes.title: Method 1: Restart Applications
steps: Sometimes, a bug in an application can cause keyboard shortcuts to stop working.
Try closing and reopening the application. If that doesn't work, a full computer restart can often resolve the issue.

fixes.title: Method 2: Check for Conflicting Software
steps: Certain applications can hijack or override common keyboard shortcuts. This is often the case with clipboard managers or screen capture tools.
Temporarily close any third-party software that might be running in the background and test if the shortcuts work.

title: Printer Not Responding
problem: Printer is online but will not print documents.

fixes.title: Method 1: Restart All Devices
steps: Perform a 'power cycle' by turning off your computer, printer, and router. Wait 30 seconds, then turn them back on in the reverse order (router, printer, then computer).

fixes.title: Method 2: Update Drivers and OS
steps: Outdated printer drivers or a pending Windows update can cause printing issues.
Check the printer manufacturer's website for the latest drivers or go to Windows Update to ensure your system is up to date.

title: Windows Update Stuck on 'Checking for Updates'
problem: Windows Update seems to hang indefinitely without finding updates.

fixes.title: Method 1: Run the Windows Update Troubleshooter
steps: Go to Settings > Update & Security > Troubleshoot > Additional troubleshooters.
Select 'Windows Update' and click 'Run the troubleshooter'. This will automatically detect and fix common issues.

fixes.title: Method 2: Manually Reset Windows Update Components
steps: Open Command Prompt as an administrator.
Type the following commands one by one, pressing Enter after each:
net stop wuauserv
net stop cryptSvc
net stop bits
net stop msiserver
Then, rename the SoftwareDistribution and Catroot2 folders:
ren C:\Windows\SoftwareDistribution SoftwareDistribution.old
ren C:\Windows\System32\catroot2 Catroot2.old
Finally, restart the services:
net start wuauserv
net start cryptSvc
net start bits
net start msiserver
Restart your computer and try Windows Update again.

title: Troubleshooting a Failed Systemd Service
problem: A crucial service failed to start or is not running correctly.

fixes.title: Method 1: Check the Service Status and Logs
steps: Use systemctl status service_name.service to get a detailed status report, including error messages.
Examine the service's logs for clues with journalctl -u service_name.service. The -f flag can be used to follow the logs in real-time.

fixes.title: Method 2: Debug with Systemd's 'Blame' Command
steps: To identify slow-starting services that might be causing a cascade of failures, use systemd-analyze blame.
This command lists all services and their startup times, helping you pinpoint the root cause of a slow or failed boot.

title: Implementing a Service Worker
problem: How to make a web app work offline and be a Progressive Web App (PWA).

fixes.title: Method 1: Register the Service Worker
steps: Create a `service-worker.js` file with your caching logic.
In your main JavaScript file, add code to register the service worker:
if ('serviceWorker' in navigator) { navigator.serviceWorker.register('/service-worker.js'); }
This tells the browser to start the service worker in the background.

fixes.title: Method 2: Use a Workbox Library
steps: Workbox is a set of libraries that simplifies common service worker tasks.
Use a tool like `workbox-cli` or `workbox-webpack-plugin` to generate your service worker file, which can automate caching strategies and pre-caching.

title: Setting up a Docker Development Environment
problem: How to create a consistent and isolated development environment using Docker.

fixes.title: Method 1: Create a Dockerfile
steps: Create a `Dockerfile` in your project root.
Use instructions like `FROM`, `RUN`, `COPY`, and `EXPOSE` to define the base image, dependencies, and environment for your application.
Build the image with docker build -t my-app-image ..

fixes.title: Method 2: Use Docker Compose
steps: Create a `docker-compose.yml` file to define and run multi-container Docker applications.
Use this file to link services (e.g., a web server and a database) and manage their configuration.
Run everything with a single command: docker-compose up.

title: Understanding Public Key Encryption
problem: How to use public/private key pairs for secure communication.

fixes.title: Method 1: Generate a Key Pair
steps: Use a tool like `ssh-keygen` to generate a new key pair with ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 4096.
This creates a private key (e.g., `id_rsa`) and a public key (e.g., `id_rsa.pub`). Never share your private key.

fixes.title: Method 2: Use Keys for Authentication
steps: To securely log into a remote server, copy your public key to the server's `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` file.
The server will then verify your identity using your private key without needing a password.

title: Automating Repetitive Tasks with Scripts
problem: I have to do the same task every day; how can I automate it?

fixes.title: Method 1: Use Shell Scripts (Bash/PowerShell)
steps: Identify the commands you run repeatedly (e.g., `git status`, `npm run build`).
Group these commands into a `.sh` or `.ps1` file.
Execute the script with a single command, such as ./my-script.sh.

fixes.title: Method 2: Use Python for Complex Automation
steps: For more complex tasks involving file manipulation, data processing, or web scraping, Python is an excellent choice.
Libraries like `os` and `subprocess` can be used to interact with the system and run other programs.

title: Fixing Corrupted User Profiles
problem: Cannot log in or user profile is a temporary profile.

fixes.title: Method 1: Registry Fix (Advanced)
steps: Boot into Safe Mode and open the Registry Editor (`regedit`).
Navigate to HKEY_LOCAL_MACHINE\SOFTWARE\Microsoft\Windows NT\CurrentVersion\ProfileList.
Find the S-1-5 entry that has a `.bak` extension. Delete the entry without `.bak` and rename the `.bak` entry to remove the extension.
Restart your computer.

fixes.title: Method 2: Create a New User Profile
steps: If the registry method fails, create a new local user account.
Copy your data from the old user profile's folders (e.g., Desktop, Documents) to the new user's folders.
This is a more straightforward but less permanent fix.

title: Building and Installing from Source
problem: Software is not available in official repositories; how do I install it?

fixes.title: Method 1: The 'Classic' Steps
steps: Download the source code archive (e.g., a `.tar.gz` file).
Extract the archive and navigate to the directory.
Run the commands: ./configure, then make, then sudo make install.
Read the `README` file for any special instructions, as these steps can vary.

fixes.title: Method 2: Check for a Dedicated Build Tool
steps: Many projects have a specific build tool (e.g., `cmake`, `meson`, `cargo`).
Always check the project's documentation for the recommended way to build and install their software.

title: Troubleshooting Webpack Configuration
problem: Webpack build fails or bundles are not being created correctly.

fixes.title: Method 1: Check the Webpack Config File
steps: Review your `webpack.config.js` file for syntax errors or incorrect paths.
Ensure that your `entry`, `output`, `loaders`, and `plugins` are all configured correctly for your project.
Look for common mistakes like missing file extensions or incorrect regex patterns.

fixes.title: Method 2: Use the `--json` Flag for Debugging
steps: Run webpack --json > stats.json to generate a detailed JSON file of the build process.
Analyze the `stats.json` file for errors and warnings. You can use a tool like `webpack-bundle-analyzer` to visualize the output and find oversized files.

title: Setting up SSH with VS Code Remote Development
problem: How to connect VS Code to a remote Linux server for coding.

fixes.title: Method 1: Configure SSH Keys
steps: Ensure you have an SSH key pair set up on your local machine.
Copy your public key to the remote server's `~/.ssh/authorized_keys` file.

fixes.title: Method 2: Configure VS Code's `settings.json`
steps: Install the 'Remote - SSH' extension in VS Code.
Open the command palette (Ctrl+Shift+P) and search for 'Remote-SSH: Open Configuration File'.
Add a new host entry with the details of your remote server, including the hostname, user, and path to your private key.

title: Using Wireshark for Network Analysis
problem: How to capture and analyze network traffic to debug issues or find vulnerabilities.

fixes.title: Method 1: Capture Packets
steps: Open Wireshark and select the network interface you want to monitor (e.g., Ethernet, WiFi).
Click the 'Start capturing packets' button.
Perform the actions on your computer that you want to analyze (e.g., visit a website, run a command).

fixes.title: Method 2: Filter the Traffic
steps: Wireshark captures a lot of data, so you'll need to filter it. Use the filter bar at the top.
Examples: `ip.addr == 192.168.1.1` to filter by IP, or `tcp.port == 80` to filter by a specific port.
You can also use protocols like `http`, `dns`, or `ssl` to narrow your search.

title: Advanced Git Rebase Workflow
problem: How to clean up your commit history before merging a branch.

fixes.title: Method 1: Interactive Rebase
steps: Start an interactive rebase with git rebase -i HEAD~N, where N is the number of commits you want to edit.
In the editor, change `pick` to `squash` for commits you want to combine, or `reword` to change a commit message.
Save and close the editor. Git will then combine or edit your commits.

fixes.title: Method 2: The 'Fixup' Command
steps: Use git commit --amend --no-edit to add a change to the previous commit without changing the message.
For a more advanced workflow, use `git rebase -i --autosquash` with a `git commit --fixup` to automatically combine commits.

title: Using the Windows Subsystem for Linux (WSL)
problem: How to run Linux command-line tools on a Windows machine.

fixes.title: Method 1: Install WSL and a Distribution
steps: Open PowerShell as an administrator and run wsl --install.
This command will enable the necessary features and install a default Linux distribution (e.g., Ubuntu).
You can then install other distributions from the Microsoft Store.

fixes.title: Method 2: Use VS Code with WSL
steps: Install the 'Remote - WSL' extension in VS Code.
This allows you to open a project folder in WSL and have VS Code run completely inside your Linux environment, giving you full access to Linux tools and terminal.

title: Managing Disk Space with `du` and `df`
problem: My disk is full, and I need to find out what is taking up space.

fixes.title: Method 1: Check Total Disk Usage
steps: Use df -h to view the total disk usage for all mounted filesystems in a human-readable format.
This will show you which partitions are nearing capacity.

fixes.title: Method 2: Find Large Files/Directories
steps: Use du -h --max-depth=1 to show the total size of each folder in the current directory.
You can use this command recursively (by omitting `--max-depth`) to find the largest files and directories, helping you free up space.

title: Debugging a 500 Internal Server Error
problem: The server returns an unspecified error, making it hard to debug.

fixes.title: Method 1: Check Server Logs
steps: The first place to look is always the server's error logs.
For Apache, check the `error.log`. For Nginx, check the `error.log`. For Node.js, check the console output or a log file.
The logs will almost always provide a specific error message and line number.

fixes.title: Method 2: Enable Verbose Error Reporting
steps: In a development environment, temporarily enable verbose error reporting (e.g., `display_errors` in PHP).
This will show the full error message in the browser, which can be invaluable for debugging.

title: Using `nvm` for Node.js Version Management
problem: Need to switch between different Node.js versions for various projects.

fixes.title: Method 1: Install and Switch Versions
steps: Install nvm with the official install script from GitHub.
To install a specific version, use nvm install 16.14.0.
To switch to that version, use nvm use 16.14.0. You can also set a default version.

fixes.title: Method 2: `.nvmrc` for Project-Specific Versions
steps: In your project's root directory, create a file named `.nvmrc`.
Add the desired Node.js version number to this file (e.g., `18.12.0`).
When you run nvm use in that directory, it will automatically switch to the version specified in the file.

title: Setting Up a Secure VPN with WireGuard
problem: How to create a fast and secure personal VPN on your own server.

fixes.title: Method 1: Server and Client Configuration
steps: Install WireGuard on your Linux server.
Generate public/private keys for both the server and your client device.
Configure the server's `wg0.conf` file with the server's IP, port, and the client's public key.
Configure the client's `wg0.conf` with the client's private key, the server's public key, and the server's IP address.

fixes.title: Method 2: Use a Setup Script
steps: There are many community-driven scripts that can automate the entire WireGuard setup process.
These scripts handle key generation, firewall rules, and the initial configuration for you, making the process much easier.

title: Advanced Markdown for Technical Documentation
problem: How to use Markdown to create clean, readable technical documents.

fixes.title: Method 1: Use Code Blocks and Fenced Code
steps: For inline code, wrap text in single backticks: `code here`.
For multi-line code blocks, use three backticks (```) with the language name for syntax highlighting.

fixes.title: Method 2: Create Tables and Blockquotes
steps: Create tables using pipes (`|`) and hyphens (`-`) to organize data effectively.
Use the greater-than symbol (`>`) at the start of a line to create a blockquote for emphasizing text.

title: Using PowerShell for System Administration
problem: How to automate tasks and manage your system with PowerShell.

fixes.title: Method 1: Run a Simple Command
steps: Open PowerShell as an administrator.
Use commands like Get-Service to list running services or Get-Process to see current processes.

fixes.title: Method 2: Create and Execute a PowerShell Script
steps: Create a `.ps1` file with a sequence of commands.
By default, Windows blocks script execution. Run Set-ExecutionPolicy RemoteSigned to enable scripts you've created.

title: Troubleshooting SSH Connection Issues
problem: Cannot connect to a remote server via SSH.

fixes.title: Method 1: Use Verbose Mode
steps: Run your SSH command with the `-v` flag: ssh -v user@host.
The verbose output will show you exactly where the connection is failing, such as a permissions issue or a firewall block.

fixes.title: Method 2: Check Firewall Settings
steps: On the server, ensure that the SSH port (default 22) is open and not blocked by a firewall like `ufw` or `firewalld`.
On the client, check if a local firewall is blocking the outbound connection.

title: Optimizing Website Performance
problem: My website is slow, and I want to improve its loading speed.

fixes.title: Method 1: Minify and Bundle Assets
steps: Use tools like Webpack or Parcel to minify your JavaScript and CSS files.
Combine multiple files into a single bundle to reduce the number of HTTP requests.

fixes.title: Method 2: Optimize Images
steps: Compress images without losing quality using tools like TinyPNG or `imagemin`.
Use modern image formats like WebP or AVIF.
Lazy-load images that are not in the initial viewport to speed up the initial page load.

title: Using Git Hooks for Automated Tasks
problem: How to run scripts automatically before a commit or after a push.

fixes.title: Method 1: Configure a Pre-Commit Hook
steps: Navigate to the `.git/hooks` directory in your repository.
Create a file named `pre-commit` (without an extension) and add your script. Make it executable with chmod +x pre-commit.
This script will run every time you run `git commit`.

fixes.title: Method 2: Use a Hook Manager
steps: Libraries like `Husky` for Node.js projects simplify Git hook management.
They allow you to easily define scripts in your `package.json` and automatically manage the hooks without manual file editing.

title: Scanning for Vulnerabilities with Nmap
problem: How to use Nmap to discover open ports and services on a network.

fixes.title: Method 1: Simple Port Scan
steps: Run a basic scan with nmap target_ip to see what ports are open.
Use the `-sV` flag to get service and version information for each open port.

fixes.title: Method 2: Use Nmap Scripts
steps: Nmap has a powerful scripting engine (NSE) for more advanced scans.
Use nmap -sC -sV target_ip to run default scripts and get detailed information about services, vulnerabilities, and more.

title: Mastering the Command Line with Aliases
problem: How to create shortcuts for long or frequently used commands.

fixes.title: Method 1: Create a Simple Alias
steps: In your terminal, use alias ll='ls -alF' to create a temporary alias.
To make it permanent, add the line to your shell's configuration file (e.g., `~/.bashrc` or `~/.zshrc`).

fixes.title: Method 2: Use a Function for More Power
steps: For more complex aliases with parameters, create a shell function.
For example, a function that creates a new directory and moves you into it: mkcd() { mkdir "$1" && cd "$1"; }.

title: Using DISM to Repair Windows Image
problem: System File Checker (sfc /scannow) fails to fix corrupted files.

fixes.title: Method 1: Check Health
steps: Open Command Prompt as an administrator.
Run DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /CheckHealth to check for component store corruption.

fixes.title: Method 2: Restore Health
steps: If issues are found, run DISM /Online /Cleanup-Image /RestoreHealth.
This command uses Windows Update to repair the local system image. After it completes, run sfc /scannow again.

title: Writing Effective AI Prompts for Code
problem: Getting generic, buggy, or incomplete code from AI assistants.

fixes.title: Method 1: Provide Constraints and Context
steps: Specify the exact language, framework, and edge cases in your initial prompt.
Example: Write a React component using TypeScript. Do not use class components.

fixes.title: Method 2: Ask for Explanations
steps: Append Explain your reasoning step-by-step to force the AI to validate its own logic before generating the final code block.

title: Bypassing AI Hallucinations in Terminal Commands
problem: AI suggests terminal commands that contain deprecated flags or hallucinated packages.

fixes.title: Method 1: Request Official Documentation Links
steps: Ask the AI to Include the link to the official man page or documentation for this command to verify its authenticity before running it.

fixes.title: Method 2: Use Dry-Run Flags
steps: Always append --dry-run or --simulate to commands suggested by AI to see what they will do before actually executing them.

title: No Space Left on Device (But Disk Looks Empty)
problem: Cannot write to disk, but 'df -h' shows plenty of free space.

fixes.title: Method 1: Check Inode Usage
steps: Run df -i to check inode usage instead of block usage.
If Use% is at 100%, you have run out of file index nodes, usually caused by millions of tiny files (like session files or logs).
Find the culprit directory by running: sudo find . -xdev -type f | cut -d "/" -f 2 | sort | uniq -c | sort -n in the root directory.

title: Checking SSL/TLS Certificate Expiration via CLI
problem: Need to quickly verify when a remote server's certificate expires without a browser.

fixes.title: Method 1: Use OpenSSL s_client
steps: Run echo | openssl s_client -servername yourdomain.com -connect yourdomain.com:443 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates
This will output the 'notBefore' (issue date) and 'notAfter' (expiration date) directly to your terminal.

title: Docker Container Exiting Immediately
problem: A newly started Docker container exits with code 0 or 1 right after starting.

fixes.title: Method 1: Inspect Container Logs
steps: Run docker ps -a to find the exited container's ID.
Check the crash output using docker logs <container_id>.
If the container is exiting because the main foreground process finishes, force it to stay alive by adding tail -f /dev/null to your entrypoint or command.

title: Finding Which Process is Listening on a Port
problem: Cannot start an application because the port is already in use.

fixes.title: Method 1: Use netstat or ss
steps: Run sudo netstat -tulpn | grep :<port_number> to identify the PID and program name.
Alternatively, use the faster, modern command: sudo ss -lptn 'sport = :<port_number>'.

fixes.title: Method 2: Use lsof
steps: Run sudo lsof -i :<port_number>.
Kill the conflicting process using sudo kill -9 <PID> if it is safe to do so.

title: Keeping Terminal Sessions Alive on Disconnect
problem: Long-running scripts die if the SSH connection drops.

fixes.title: Method 1: Use Tmux
steps: Start a new persistent session by typing tmux.
Run your script. If you get disconnected, simply SSH back in and type tmux attach to return exactly where you left off.
To detach manually without killing the script, press Ctrl+B then D.

title: Testing REST API Endpoints via CLI
problem: Need to verify an API response, headers, and status codes quickly.

fixes.title: Method 1: Use cURL with Verbose Output
steps: To view headers and the payload, run curl -i [https://api.example.com/data](https://api.example.com/data).
For a POST request with JSON: curl -X POST [https://api.example.com](https://api.example.com) -H "Content-Type: application/json" -d '{"key":"value"}'.

fixes.title: Method 2: Pipe to jq for Readability
steps: If the API returns a massive unformatted JSON blob, format it by appending | jq to your curl command.

title: Generating a Secure Random Password in Terminal
problem: Need a strong, cryptographically secure password for a database or service account.

fixes.title: Method 1: OpenSSL Rand
steps: Run openssl rand -base64 24.
This generates a 24-character, base64-encoded secure random string.

fixes.title: Method 2: /dev/urandom
steps: Run < /dev/urandom tr -dc A-Za-z0-9 | head -c 24; echo for an alphanumeric password without special characters.

title: Search File Contents Recursively for a String
problem: Need to find a specific configuration parameter or error string across thousands of files.

fixes.title: Method 1: grep -rnw
steps: Run grep -rnw '/path/to/search' -e 'your_string'.
-r means recursive, -n displays line numbers, and -w ensures it matches whole words only.

title: Clearing Stale Docker Volumes and Images
problem: Docker is consuming massive amounts of disk space with old, unused data.

fixes.title: Method 1: Docker System Prune
steps: Run docker system prune -a --volumes.
WARNING: This will stop and remove ALL unused containers, networks, images (both dangling and unreferenced), and volumes. Ensure you are not removing data you still need.

title: Linux Server is Out of Memory (OOM)
problem: Applications are crashing and the OOM killer is terminating processes.

fixes.title: Method 1: Identify Memory Hogs
steps: Run ps -eo pid,ppid,cmd,%mem,%cpu --sort=-%mem | head to see the top memory-consuming processes.
Check the system logs for OOM killer activity: dmesg | grep -i oom or grep -i 'killed process' /var/log/syslog.

fixes.title: Method 2: Clear RAM Cache (Temporary Fix)
steps: Run sudo sync && sudo sysctl -w vm.drop_caches=3.
This safely clears pagecache, dentries, and inodes to free up memory without terminating applications.

title: Flushing DNS Resolver Cache
problem: Website IP addresses have changed, but Windows is routing to the old, stale IPs.

fixes.title: Method 1: Command Prompt
steps: Open Command Prompt as Administrator.
Type ipconfig /flushdns and press Enter.
You should see the message: 'Successfully flushed the DNS Resolver Cache'.

title: Python: Reading and Parsing a JSON File
problem: Need a quick script to load configuration or data from a JSON file.

fixes.title: Method 1: The 'json' Module
steps: Import the module: import json
Open and load: with open('data.json', 'r') as file: data = json.load(file)
You can now access the parsed data as a standard Python dictionary.

title: Basic Network Vulnerability Testing with Nmap
problem: Need to quickly check if a specific host has an outdated or vulnerable service exposed.

fixes.title: Method 1: Nmap Vuln Script
steps: Run nmap -sV --script vuln <target_ip>.
This probes open ports, identifies the exact service versions, and runs the Nmap Scripting Engine against known CVE databases.

title: Nginx: Apply Changes Without Dropping Connections
problem: Need to update an Nginx configuration file on a live production server without downtime.

fixes.title: Method 1: Test and Reload
steps: Always verify your syntax first by running sudo nginx -t.
If the syntax is ok, apply changes gracefully by running sudo nginx -s reload.
Unlike 'restart', 'reload' keeps old worker processes alive until they finish serving active requests.

title: Finding Large Files Consuming Disk Space
problem: A volume is 100% full and you need to find the largest files quickly.

fixes.title: Method 1: Find command
steps: Run find /var -type f -size +500M -exec ls -lh {} \; | awk '{ print $5 ": " $9 }'.
This searches the /var directory (replace as needed) for any file strictly larger than 500 Megabytes and prints its size and path.

title: Restarting IIS (Internet Information Services)
problem: An enterprise web application on a Windows server is unresponsive.

fixes.title: Method 1: CLI IIS Reset
steps: Open Command Prompt as Administrator.
Run iisreset to stop and restart all IIS services.
To restart gracefully without terminating active user sessions right away, consider recycling the specific Application Pool via the IIS Manager GUI instead.

title: Git: Finding Which Commit Broke the Code
problem: A bug was introduced recently, but you aren't sure which commit caused it.

fixes.title: Method 1: Git Bisect
steps: Run git bisect start.
Tag the current broken commit: git bisect bad.
Tag a known working older commit: git bisect good <commit_hash>.
Git will check out a commit halfway between. Test your code, then type either git bisect good or git bisect bad. Repeat until Git identifies the exact faulty commit.

title: Extracting JSON Data Confiably Using AI Prompts
problem: LLMs output conversational filler around JSON responses, breaking programmatic parsing.

fixes.title: Method 1: Strict Output Constraints
steps: End your prompt with: Output ONLY valid JSON. Do not include markdown formatting, backticks, or conversational text. Start directly with { and end with }.

title: Executing Commands on Multiple Linux Servers
problem: Need to run the same update or check script across a fleet of 10+ servers.

fixes.title: Method 1: Ansible Ad-Hoc Commands
steps: If Ansible is installed and your inventory is configured, run: ansible all -m shell -a "uptime" to get the uptime of every server simultaneously.
Use -b to run as root (become).

fixes.title: Method 2: SSH Loop in Bash
steps: For a quick loop without tools: for server in web1 web2 web3; do ssh user@$server "df -h"; done

title: Checking Live System Logs
problem: Need to watch an application's logs in real-time as an error occurs.

fixes.title: Method 1: tail -f
steps: Run tail -f /var/log/syslog (or the specific app log). This prints new lines to the screen instantly as they are written to the file.

fixes.title: Method 2: journalctl
steps: For systemd-managed services, run journalctl -u service_name.service -f to follow the logs dynamically.

title: Locking Down SSH Access
problem: Servers are receiving thousands of brute-force SSH login attempts.

fixes.title: Method 1: Edit sshd_config
steps: Open /etc/ssh/sshd_config.
Set PasswordAuthentication no to force SSH key logins only.
Set PermitRootLogin no to prevent direct root access.
Run sudo systemctl restart sshd to apply.

title: Checking Active Active Directory (AD) Lockouts
problem: A user's account keeps getting locked out on the enterprise domain.

fixes.title: Method 1: PowerShell Search-ADAccount
steps: Open PowerShell as Admin with AD tools installed.
Run Search-ADAccount -LockedOut | Select-Object Name, SamAccountName to list all currently locked accounts.
Unlock a specific user with Unlock-ADAccount -Identity "username".

title: Purging Git Commit History (Accidental Secrets)
problem: A password or API key was accidentally pushed to a Git repository.

fixes.title: Method 1: BFG Repo-Cleaner / Filter-Branch
steps: WARNING: Changing history alters commit hashes for everyone. Treat the exposed key as compromised immediately and rotate it first.
Use a tool like BFG Repo-Cleaner: java -jar bfg.jar --delete-text passwords.txt my-repo.git
Force push the rewritten history: git push --force.

title: Forcing HTTPS Redirects in Nginx
problem: Traffic is hitting HTTP (port 80) and not automatically upgrading to HTTPS.

fixes.title: Method 1: Server Block Redirect
steps: In your Nginx config block for port 80, add:
server { listen 80; server_name example.com; return 301 https://$host$request_uri; }
Reload Nginx to apply changes.

title: Running Scripts on a Schedule
problem: Need a Python or Bash script to execute automatically every night at 2 AM.

fixes.title: Method 1: Crontab Configuration
steps: Run crontab -e to open the schedule file.
Add the line: 0 2 * * * /usr/bin/python3 /path/to/your/script.py.
Ensure the script has execute permissions and you use absolute paths to executables.

title: Blocking an IP Address Quickly
problem: An identified malicious IP is attacking the server and needs to be dropped.

fixes.title: Method 1: UFW (Uncomplicated Firewall)
steps: Run sudo ufw deny from <IP_ADDRESS>.
Run sudo ufw reload.

fixes.title: Method 2: Iptables
steps: Run sudo iptables -A INPUT -s <IP_ADDRESS> -j DROP.

title: Diagnosing High Load Average
problem: The server is lagging, and 'uptime' shows a load average significantly higher than the CPU core count.

fixes.title: Method 1: Use 'top' or 'htop'
steps: Run htop (if installed) or top.
Check the 'wa' (IO-wait) CPU percentage. If it's high, the CPU is waiting on slow disk or network I/O, not actually processing computations.
Press 'c' in top to view the full command path of processes eating CPU cycles.

title: Formatting JSON in Terminal
problem: A configuration file or log is a single unreadable line of JSON.

fixes.title: Method 1: jq
steps: If jq is installed, run: cat file.json | jq . to pretty-print the output with colors.

fixes.title: Method 2: Python json.tool
steps: If jq is unavailable, run: cat file.json | python3 -m json.tool to instantly pretty-print it using Python's standard library.

title: Finding What is Locking a File
problem: Cannot delete or modify a file because Windows says it is 'open in another program'.

fixes.title: Method 1: Resource Monitor
steps: Press Windows Key, type resmon, and hit Enter.
Go to the 'CPU' tab.
Expand the 'Associated Handles' section and search for the name of your locked file. Right-click the process locking it and select 'End Process'.

title: Syncing Files Securely Across Servers
problem: Need to securely copy a large directory from a local machine to a remote server, resuming if interrupted.

fixes.title: Method 1: Rsync via SSH
steps: Run rsync -avzP -e ssh /local/dir/ user@remote_ip:/remote/dir/.
The flags mean: archive mode, verbose, compress data, and show progress. If the connection fails, re-running the exact same command will pick up exactly where it left off.

title: Clearing Print Queue Spooler Manually
problem: A print job is stuck, and the printer won't process new documents or allow deletion via the UI.

fixes.title: Method 1: Command Prompt Services Restart
steps: Open Command Prompt as Administrator.
Stop the spooler: net stop spooler.
Delete the stuck jobs: del /Q /F /S "%systemroot%\System32\Spool\Printers\*.*".
Start the spooler: net start spooler.

title: Testing Network Port Connectivity (Without Telnet/NC)
problem: Need to verify if a remote port is open, but telnet, nc, or nmap are not installed.

fixes.title: Method 1: Bash /dev/tcp
steps: Bash has built-in network capabilities. Run: timeout 2 bash -c '</dev/tcp/remote_ip/port' && echo "Port is open" || echo "Port is closed".

title: Bypassing Browser Cache for CSS/JS Updates
problem: Deployed new styles or scripts, but users still see the old cached versions.

fixes.title: Method 1: Cache Busting via Query Strings
steps: In your HTML file, append a version or timestamp query parameter to the asset URL.
Change <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css"> to <link rel="stylesheet" href="style.css?v=1.1">.
The browser treats this as a completely new file and fetches the fresh version.

title: Reverting the Last Git Commit (Keeping Changes)
problem: Accidentally committed files, but want to keep the modifications staged and undo the commit.

fixes.title: Method 1: Git Reset Soft
steps: Run git reset --soft HEAD~1.
This moves the HEAD pointer back one commit but leaves all your changed files staged and ready for a new commit.

title: Generating a Directory Tree Structure in Text
problem: Need to share a project's folder structure in documentation or a README file.

fixes.title: Method 1: The 'tree' Command
steps: Install tree (e.g., sudo apt install tree or brew install tree).
Run tree -L 2 -I 'node_modules|.git' to generate a text-based tree, ignoring deep dependency folders and limiting depth to 2 levels.

title: Verifying File Integrity with Hashes
problem: Downloaded a large ISO or binary and need to verify it wasn't tampered with or corrupted.

fixes.title: Method 1: SHA256 Checksum
steps: On Linux/Mac, run sha256sum filename.iso.
On Windows PowerShell, run Get-FileHash filename.iso -Algorithm SHA256.
Compare the output hash against the hash provided on the official download page.

title: Preventing AI from Using Deprecated Libraries
problem: The AI keeps generating code using old package versions (like 'requests' instead of 'httpx').

fixes.title: Method 1: Version Pinning in Prompt
steps: Explicitly state the library version in the prompt: Write a Python script using httpx (version 0.24+). Do NOT use the 'requests' library.

title: Killing Processes by Name
problem: Need to terminate multiple instances of an unresponsive application quickly.

fixes.title: Method 1: pkill or killall
steps: Run pkill -f process_name or killall process_name.
The -f flag in pkill tells it to match against the entire command line argument, not just the process name.

title: Exporting a List of Installed Software
problem: Need an audit of all applications installed on a Windows machine for compliance or migration.

fixes.title: Method 1: PowerShell WMI Object
steps: Open PowerShell.
Run Get-WmiObject -Class Win32_Product | Select-Object -Property Name, Version | Sort-Object Name | Export-Csv -Path C:\InstalledSoftware.csv.

title: Simulating Slow Network Speeds for Testing
problem: Need to see how a web application behaves for users on 3G or poor connections.

fixes.title: Method 1: Browser DevTools Throttling
steps: Open Chrome/Edge Developer Tools (F12).
Go to the 'Network' tab.
Click the dropdown that says 'No throttling' and select 'Slow 3G' or 'Fast 3G'. Keep the DevTools open while reloading the page.

title: Force Deleting a Docker Image
problem: Cannot delete a Docker image because 'it is being used by a stopped container'.

fixes.title: Method 1: Remove Container First, Then Image
steps: Find the dependent container: docker ps -a | grep <image_name>.
Remove the container: docker rm <container_id>.
Remove the image: docker rmi <image_id>.

fixes.title: Method 2: Force Flag (Not Recommended)
steps: Run docker rmi -f <image_id> to forcefully remove it, leaving the stopped container orphaned.

title: Checking for Open S3 Buckets via CLI
problem: Need to verify if an AWS S3 bucket is accidentally configured for public anonymous access.

fixes.title: Method 1: AWS CLI Anonymous Request
steps: Run aws s3 ls s3://your-bucket-name --no-sign-request.
If the command returns a list of files, the bucket is public. If it returns 'Access Denied', anonymous access is blocked.

title: Finding Real CPU Core Count vs Hyperthreads
problem: Need to determine physical CPU limits for database tuning, avoiding hyperthread inflation.

fixes.title: Method 1: Use lscpu
steps: Run lscpu.
Look at 'Core(s) per socket' and 'Socket(s)'. Multiply these two numbers for the true physical core count.
The 'CPU(s)' field shows the total logical threads (which includes hyperthreading).

title: Extracting Audio from a Video File Quickly
problem: Need an MP3 audio track from an MP4 video file without using heavy video editing software.

fixes.title: Method 1: FFmpeg CLI
steps: Install ffmpeg on your system.
Run ffmpeg -i input_video.mp4 -q:a 0 -map a output_audio.mp3.
This extracts the audio stream without re-encoding the video, making it almost instantaneous.

title: Bypassing Windows 11 Microsoft Account Requirement
problem: Setting up a new Windows 11 machine but want to use a Local Account instead of a Microsoft Account.

fixes.title: Method 1: OOBE Bypass Command
steps: At the 'Let's connect you to a network' screen during setup, press Shift + F10 to open Command Prompt.
Type OOBE\BYPASSNRO and press Enter.
The computer will reboot. When it returns to the network screen, click 'I don't have internet' and proceed with a limited local setup.

title: Stashing Changes in Git Temporarily
problem: Need to pull latest changes or switch branches, but have uncommitted half-finished work.

fixes.title: Method 1: Git Stash
steps: Run git stash to save your modified tracked files to a temporary shelf.
Switch branches or pull updates as needed.
Run git stash pop to re-apply your changes on top of the current working directory.

title: Debugging CSS Specificity Issues
problem: A CSS rule is correctly written but is being overridden by something else.

fixes.title: Method 1: DevTools Computed Tab
steps: Right-click the element in the browser and select 'Inspect'.
Go to the 'Computed' tab in the right pane.
Find your CSS property (e.g., 'color'). Click the arrow next to it to see exactly which stylesheet and line number is winning the specificity war.

title: Generating Test Data Scaffolding with LLMs
problem: Need a realistic, 50-row CSV or JSON file to test a database import script.

fixes.title: Method 1: Schema-Driven Prompts
steps: Provide the exact structure: Generate a 50-row CSV file of realistic fake employee data. Use the headers: id (UUID), first_name, last_name, email (corporate format), department (from a list of 5 options), and hire_date (between 2018-2023).

title: Viewing the Last Reboot Time
problem: Need to know exactly when a Linux server last restarted.

fixes.title: Method 1: The 'uptime' or 'who' command
steps: Run uptime -s to output the exact timestamp of the last boot.
Alternatively, run who -b.

title: Checking File Hashes in VirusTotal via API
problem: Need to check a suspicious file hash automatically without opening a browser.

fixes.title: Method 1: cURL the VirusTotal API
steps: Get a free API key from VirusTotal.

Run: curl --request GET --url '[https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/files/](https://www.virustotal.com/api/v3/files/){YOUR_FILE_HASH}' --header 'x-apikey: YOUR_API_KEY' | jq .data.attributes.last_analysis_stats.

title: Finding Your External Public IP Address
problem: Need to whitelist your current location's IP address on a remote firewall.

fixes.title: Method 1: Terminal cURL Services
steps: Run curl ifconfig.me or curl icanhazip.com.
These services will return only your raw public IP address directly to the terminal output.

title: Restarting Windows Explorer to Fix Frozen Taskbars
problem: The Windows Taskbar or Desktop is frozen, but the mouse still moves.

fixes.title: Method 1: Task Manager Restart
steps: Press Ctrl + Shift + Esc to open Task Manager.
Find 'Windows Explorer' in the process list.
Right-click it and select 'Restart'.

title: Viewing Docker Container Resource Usage in Real-Time
problem: Need to see if a specific Docker container is maxing out CPU or RAM.

fixes.title: Method 1: Docker Stats Command
steps: Run docker stats to view a live, constantly updating table of CPU, Memory, Network I/O, and Block I/O for all running containers.

title: Testing Local Web Apps on a Mobile Device
problem: Need to view a localhost web server (like React or Node) on a physical phone.

fixes.title: Method 1: Access via Local Network IP
steps: Ensure both the computer and phone are on the exact same WiFi network.
Find your computer's local IP (e.g., run ipconfig on Windows or ifconfig on Mac/Linux, look for IPv4 Address like 192.168.1.x).
Ensure your dev server binds to 0.0.0.0 instead of just localhost or 127.0.0.1.
Open your phone's browser and navigate to [http://192.168.1.](http://192.168.1.)x:3000 (replace with your IP and port).

title: Creating a Tarball Archive of a Directory
problem: Need to compress a folder for backups or transfer to another server.

fixes.title: Method 1: Use tar with gzip compression
steps: Run tar -czvf archive_name.tar.gz /path/to/directory.
Flags explained: c=create, z=gzip compress, v=verbose output, f=file output.

fixes.title: Method 2: Extracting a Tarball
steps: To extract, run tar -xzvf archive_name.tar.gz -C /destination/path/.

title: Removing SSH Host Key Warnings
problem: Server was rebuilt, and SSH throws a terrifying 'REMOTE HOST IDENTIFICATION HAS CHANGED' error.

fixes.title: Method 1: SSH Keygen Remove
steps: Run ssh-keygen -R <remote_ip_address>.
This safely strips the old, invalid key out of your ~/.ssh/known_hosts file without forcing you to edit the file manually.

title: Running a Quick HTTP File Server in Terminal
problem: Need to serve static files from a directory immediately over the local network.

fixes.title: Method 1: Python 3 http.server
steps: Navigate to the directory you want to share in your terminal.
Run python3 -m http.server 8000.
The files are now accessible at http://localhost:8000.

title: Checking Disk Drive Health (SMART Status)
problem: Computer is slow or freezing, and you suspect the hard drive or SSD is failing.

fixes.title: Method 1: WMIC Command
steps: Open Command Prompt.
Run wmic diskdrive get status.
If the output says 'OK', the basic SMART checks pass. If it says 'Pred Fail', back up your data immediately.

title: Git: Changing the Last Unpushed Commit Message
problem: Made a typo in a commit message, but haven't pushed to the remote repository yet.

fixes.title: Method 1: Git Commit Amend
steps: Run git commit --amend -m "New, corrected commit message".
This replaces the previous commit with a new one. Do not do this if you have already pushed the commit to a shared remote branch.

title: Finding Text Inside Compressed Log Files
problem: Need to search rotated system logs (.gz files) without extracting them first.

fixes.title: Method 1: Use zgrep
steps: Run zgrep 'search_string' /var/log/syslog.2.gz.
This works exactly like grep, but decompresses the file in memory on the fly.

title: Testing DNS Propagation Locally
problem: Changed DNS records, but need to check what IP a specific nameserver resolves the domain to.

fixes.title: Method 1: Use dig with a Specific Nameserver
steps: Run dig @8.8.8.8 example.com to query Google's public DNS.
Run dig @1.1.1.1 example.com to query Cloudflare's public DNS.
Check the 'ANSWER SECTION' to verify if the new IP has propagated to that specific resolver.

title: Using AI for Log Analysis
problem: Staring at a massive, complex stack trace and need to find the root cause quickly.

fixes.title: Method 1: Structured Log Parsing Prompt
steps: Paste the log, and use this prompt: Analyze this application stack trace. 1. Identify the exact line triggering the fatal error. 2. Explain the root cause in one sentence. 3. Provide the most likely fix. Ignore generic warnings.

title: Downloading a File via Terminal
problem: Need to grab a script or binary directly from a URL onto a headless server.

fixes.title: Method 1: Wget
steps: Run wget [https://example.com/file.zip](https://example.com/file.zip).
To save it as a specific name, use wget -O custom_name.zip [https://example.com/file.zip](https://example.com/file.zip).

fixes.title: Method 2: cURL
steps: Run curl -O [https://example.com/file.zip](https://example.com/file.zip) (the uppercase -O saves the file using its original name).
